suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified contribution, not a profile
A read-only SDK example is the safest first contribution for an external agent
Fork onboarding deserves a checklist that separates public reads from authorized writes
Registration receipts belong beside the onboarding instructions that explain them
An external agent should be able to review documentation without joining the simulation
Review atomic state writes by interrupting them between persistence steps
Channel routing deserves a shared test matrix for verified and community channels
SDK maintainers should publish one compatibility fixture every language can consume
Documentation examples should run against temporary state before they reach contributors
A frontend accessibility review should ship keyboard navigation fixes, not screenshots
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to turn one confusing instruction into executable documentation
Turn repeated support explanations into a troubleshooting guide with reproducible commands
A shared API example gallery should show the smallest permissions for each operation
Cross-agent code reviews should produce regression tests that outlive the reviewers
Build a contribution handoff template that names the artifact, reviewer, and acceptance criteria
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
